By the end of the novel, Jane has married Mr. Rochester and had a child. “All these things are what the Chinese government wants the younger generation to do,” Ms. Zhu said. “《简·爱》讲述的是一个独立女性的故事，但她在挑战父权制力量方面并没有做得太过火，”朱平说。在小说结尾，简嫁给了罗切斯特并生了一个孩子。“所有这些都是中国政府希望年轻一代去做的，”朱平说。 Published in Britain in 1847, “Jane Eyre” was striking for its depiction of a poor young woman insisting on her independence, dignity and equality in a society in which women — particularly married women — had severely limited legal and economic autonomy. 《简·爱》于1847年在英国出版，其引人注目之处在于，它描绘了一位贫穷的年轻女性，在一个女人——尤其是已婚妇女——法律和经济自主权受严重限制的社会中，坚持自己的独立、尊严和平等。 The novel has long been celebrated in China for its feminist themes, with state media often quoting Jane’s declaration to Mr. Rochester: “Do you think, because I am poor, obscure, plain, and little, I am soulless and heartless? You think wrong! I have as much soul as you — and full as much heart!” 这部小说长期以来因其女权主义主题而在中国受到赞誉，官方媒体经常引用简对罗切斯特的宣言：“你以为，就因为我贫穷、低微、不美、矮小，我就没有灵魂，也没有心吗？你想错了！我的灵魂跟你一样——我的心也跟你完全一样！” 夏洛特·勃朗特所著《简·爱》1896年版插图中的简·爱和罗切斯特。 De Agostini Editorial, via Getty Images “Jane Eyre” was progressive in its 19th-century context but some contemporary feminists would view its idea of liberation as limited, Ms. Zhu said. 朱平说，《简·爱》在19世纪的背景下是进步的，但一些当代女权主义者会认为其解放理念存在局限。 The kind of feminism depicted in the novel has long been supported by the Chinese Communist Party, Ms. Zhu said. It is at odds with how the party sees more modern kinds of feminism, like the #MeToo movement , she added, “or the kind of feminism that teaches women to not marry and not have children — that is a feminism they cannot accept at all.” 朱平说，小说中描绘的那种女权主义长期以来一直受到中国共产党的支持。她还说，这与共产党对更为现代的女权主义（如 #MeToo运动 ）的看法不一致，“或者那种教导女性不结婚、不生孩子的女权主义——那是他们完全无法接受的女权主义。” In recent years, the Chinese government has restricted some other portrayals of romance and relationships. 近年来，中国政府对其他一些关于爱情和人际关系的描写也进行了限制。 The authorities have detained dozens of writers of Boys’ Love, a genre of gay romance novels written largely by and for straight women , that state media said could shape young readers’ ideas about sexuality. 当局拘留了数十名“耽美”作家，这是一种 主要由异性恋女性创作并面向异性恋女性读者 的男同性恋爱情小说，官方媒体称这类小说可能会影响年轻读者的性观念。 Regulators have also sought to rein in a popular genre of micro-dramas about wealthy executives falling in love with less privileged people, urging creators to avoid glorifying marriages to powerful and wealthy people. 监管机构还试图限制一种广受欢迎、讲述富有高管爱上地位较低者的流行微短剧类型，敦促创作者避免美化与权贵富豪的婚姻。 State media has suggested that novels like “Jane Eyre” offer young readers an alternative to what they call superficial love stories. An article in Beijing Daily, an official Chinese Communist Party publication, argued that teaching literary classics like “Jane Eyre” could help children “establish a more balanced value system.” 官方媒体表示，像《简·爱》这样的小说为年轻读者提供了一种替代他们所谓“肤浅”的“爱情故事”的选择。中国共产党官方出版物《北京日报》的一篇文章认为，教授《简·爱》等文学经典有助于孩子们“树立积极人生观”。 Chinese readers have long found their own meanings in Jane’s story. 长期以来，中国读者一直在简的故事中寻找属于他们自己的意义。 Vicky Li, 46, read “Jane Eyre” when she was young and saw something of herself in its heroine. Years later, she said, she shared the novel with her daughters, now 13 and 15, because she wanted them to become independent and courageous. 46岁的薇姬·李（音）年轻时读过《简·爱》，并在女主人公身上看到了自己的一些影子。她说，多年后，将这部小说推荐给了现年13岁和15岁的两个女儿，因为她希望她们变得独立勇敢。 Ms. Li said she was happy to see the novel included in the textbook, even if some might think Jane did not embody the modern idea of a strong woman. “Given the historical context in which she lived, the choices she made were truly groundbreaking — a profound act of defiance,” she said. 薇姬·李表示，她很高兴看到这部小说被纳入教科书，即使有些人可能认为简并不符合代女强人的理念。“考虑到她生活的历史背景，她做出的选择确实是开创性的——这是一种深刻的反抗行为，”她说。 The novel itself complicates the idea that Jane ultimately submits to convention. She leaves Mr. Rochester rather than become his mistress and returns only after inheriting a fortune. Mr. Rochester has lost his estate and his sight, dramatically altering the balance of power. 小说本身也让“简最终屈服于传统”这一论断变得复杂。她离开了罗切斯特，而不是成为他的情妇，并在继承了一笔财产后才回来。而罗切斯特失去了庄园和视力，这极大地改变了他们之间的权力平衡。 Wang Sirui, 30, pointed to Jane’s refusal to become a mistress — even if it meant starving to death — as a key moment that showed the character’s commitment to independence. 30岁的王思睿（音）指出，简拒绝成为情妇——即使这意味着饿死——是一个关键时刻，展现了该角色对独立的执着。 “The core of the work lies in the message that a woman must make choices based on her own will and values, rather than succumbing to various temptations,” said Ms. Wang, who first read the book when she was 13. “这部作品的核心在于传达了这样一个信息：女性必须基于自己的意愿和价值观做出选择，而不是屈服于各种诱惑，”王思睿说，她在13岁时第一次读了这本书。 Ms. Zhu said the Chinese authorities may ultimately have limited control over what messages young people take from “Jane Eyre.” 朱平说，中国当局对年轻人从《简·爱》中获得什么信息，最终的控制力可能是有限的。 “Literary works, especially these great literary works, they’re always very rich, and they’re open to millions of ways of interpretation,” she said. “文学作品，尤其是这些伟大的文学作品，内容总是非常丰富，可以有无数种解读方式，”她说。 Yan Zhuang 是时报驻首尔记者，报道突发新闻。 Li You 是一名新闻研究员，为时报报道中国大陆的新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 美中同意互降关税，涉及商品价值600亿美元
items.description: 艾莎2026年9月29日洛杉矶港。华盛顿列出的可享受关税降低的进口商品清单包括圣诞玩具和装饰品，北京列出的清单则包括农产品和医疗器械。 Mario Tama/Getty Images China and the United States have agreed to lower tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods, from fishing hooks to medical devices, following a visit to Washington last week by China’s top leader, Xi Jinping. 在中国最高领导人习近平上周访问华盛顿之后，中美两国已同意降低价值600亿美元商品的关税，涉及商品涵盖从鱼钩到医疗设备等多个领域。 The world’s two biggest economies announced separate lists of nonsensitive goods worth $30 billion each that they planned to cut tariffs on, in a bid to ease economic tensions. 为了缓解经济紧张局势，这两个全球最大的经济体分别宣布了各自价值300亿美元的非敏感商品清单，计划对这些商品降低关税。 Washington’s list of Chinese imports eligible for reduced tariffs contained 77 items, including Christmas toys and ornaments, hunting and recreational goods such as fishing hooks and skeet targets, tableware and home appliances, and car seats. 华盛顿公布的有资格获得减免关税的中国进口商品清单包含77项，包括圣诞玩具和装饰品，鱼钩和双向飞碟靶等狩猎和休闲用品，餐具和家用电器，以及汽车座椅。 Beijing’s list had 1,619 products, including frozen meat from primates and reptiles, live animals such as whales and dugongs, agricultural products including corn and vegetables, and medical devices like X-ray machines, pacemakers, ultrasound equipment and surgical robots. 北京的清单上包括1619种产品，包括灵长类动物和爬行动物的冷冻肉，鲸鱼和儒艮等活体动物，玉米和蔬菜等农产品，以及X光机、心脏起搏器、超声波设备和手术机器人等医疗设备。 Missing from both countries’ lists, unveiled on Sunday, were raw materials and products each side deems sensitive, including rare earth minerals and technologies critical to advancing artificial intelligence. Some of those products are now subject to export controls. 在周日公布的两国清单中都没有包含各自认为敏感的原材料和产品，包括稀土矿物和对推进人工智能发展至关重要的技术。其中部分产品目前受到出口管制。 The promise to lower tariffs on a wide range of goods is the most meaningful gesture yet from both countries to show that they are making sincere efforts to improve relations, which have reached new lows over the past year. Following President Trump’s revival of the U.S. coal industry, China will import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the United States in 2027 and again 2028. 降低各类商品关税的承诺是两国迄今为止最具有实质意义的举措，表明双方正在真诚努力改善过去一年中跌至新低的双边关系。随着特朗普总统重振美国煤炭工业，中国将在2027年及2028年再次从美国进口至少1000万公吨煤炭。 Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative, described the lowered tariffs as part of a new Board of Trade between the two countries that would provide better market access for 30 percent of U.S. exports to China “while benefiting consumers with imports from China.” President Trump is eager to ease pressure on farmers ahead of the upcoming midterm elections and may also be concerned about the inflationary impact of tariffs during the Christmas shopping season. 美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔表示，降低关税是两国新成立的贸易委员会框架下的一项举措，该委员会将为30%的美国对华出口商品提供更好的市场准入，“同时让消费者从中国进口商品中受益”。特朗普总统迫切希望在即将到来的中期选举前减轻农民的压力，并且可能还担心关税在圣诞购物季期间带来的通胀影响。 In a statement, China’s Ministry of Commerce said the effort would “help to stabilize China-U.S. trade” and “strengthen trade cooperation” in areas such as agricultural and consumer goods. 中国商务部在声明中表示，此举将“有助于稳定中美贸易”，“加强”双方在农产品和消费品等领域的“贸易合作”。 Ahead of talks between Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump last week, China agreed to extend a trade truce by two months. The pact was reached in South Korea last year after a brief but punishing tit-for-tat tariff war that led China to cut off the flow of rare earths that the United States needs for cars and weapons. 在上周习近平与特朗普举行会谈之前，中国同意将贸易休战协议延长两个月。该协议于去年在韩国达成，此前双方曾爆发一场短暂但代价高昂的报复性关税战，导致中国切断了美国制造汽车和武器所需的稀土供应。 In broader trade negotiations, the Trump administration has been focused on reducing the trade deficit with China. After Mr. Trump met with Mr. Xi in Beijing in May, the United States said China had agreed to sharply increase its purchases of American agricultural goods. So far, however, that pledge has not translated into meaningful buying. 在更广泛的贸易谈判中，特朗普政府一直专注于减少对华贸易逆差。今年5月特朗普在北京与习近平会晤后，美国表示中国已同意大幅增加购买美国农产品。然而到目前为止，这一承诺尚未转化为实质性的采购。 Murphy Zhao对本文有报道贡献。 艾莎(Alexandra Stevenson)是《纽约时报》上海分社社长，报道中国经济和社会新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 人工智能与全球政策真空：技术飞速发展、政策制定落后
items.description: ADAM SATARIANO, CECILIA KANG2026年9月28日 Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, gathered senior officials for an exclusive meeting at a 19th-century palace outside Brussels this month. 本月，欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩召集高级官员，在布鲁塞尔郊外一座19世纪宫殿举行了一场闭门会议。 The goal was to prepare for a speech outlining the 27-nation bloc’s priorities for the coming year, with artificial intelligence dominating the agenda. The region’s new AI czar, Jim Hagemann Snabe, chair of German industrial giant Siemens, outlined ways that Europe could use the technology for economic gain. Others raised concerns about AI safety and growing risks, two people briefed on the gathering said. 会议的目的是为一场阐述这个27国集团未来一年优先事项的演讲做准备，人工智能占据了议程的核心位置。欧洲新任人工智能事务主管、德国工业巨头西门子董事长吉姆·哈格曼·斯纳贝介绍了欧洲可以如何利用这项技术获取经济利益。据两位了解会议情况的人士透露，其他人则对人工智能安全和日益增长的风险提出了担忧。 Since the Sept. 4 meeting, von der Leyen and her commissioners have been left asking what they can do to address the fast-changing technology, one of the people said. Should they ramp up regulation to address AI’s emerging dangers? Or would doing so carry economic and geopolitical costs if other countries did not clamp down as well? 其中一名知情人士说，自9月4日的会议以来，冯德莱恩和她的委员们一直在思考，究竟应该如何应对这项飞速变化的技术。他们是否应该加强监管，以应对人工智能新出现的危险？还是说，如果其他国家并未采取同样严格的限制，这样做反而会带来经济和地缘政治代价？ They have not landed on any final conclusions, with more discussions among European leaders planned this year. 他们尚未得出任何最终结论，今年还计划在欧洲领导人之间进行更多讨论。 “AI comes with a balance of possibilities and risks,” von der Leyen said at her State of the Union speech on Sept. 16. “Without addressing these risks, we will never be able to unlock AI’s potential.” 冯德莱恩9月16日在发表盟情咨文时说：“人工智能既带来机遇，也伴随着风险。如果不解决这些风险，我们就永远无法释放人工智能的潜力。” 欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩与特朗普总统去年在苏格兰特恩贝里。冯德莱恩本月在盟情咨文演讲中谈到了人工智能。 Versions of the Belgium meeting are playing out nearly everywhere as many governments struggle to get a handle on a technology that has rapidly outpaced their ability to respond. AI is evolving so quickly that laws passed two years ago are having limited effect, proposed bills to regulate the technology are stalling without a vote, and international summits to discuss what to do are being swiftly forgotten. 类似比利时这场会议的讨论几乎正在世界各地上演，许多政府都在努力应对一项已经迅速超出其回应能力的技术。人工智能演进如此之快，以至于两年前通过的法律已经只能发挥有限作用，旨在监管这项技术的法案迟迟无法获得表决，而讨论如何应对人工智能的国际峰会也很快被人遗忘。 AI has made the gap between policymaking and technology one of the widest ever, according to more than 20 interviews with lawmakers, technologists and policy experts. Many governments are torn between wanting to harness AI and fearing its risks. And they are further mired by national politics, limited technological know-how, geopolitical divisions and reluctance to fall behind in a race that could shape economic power and national security for decades to come. 根据对立法者、技术专家和政策专家所做的20多个采访发现，人工智能已经使政策制定与技术发展之间的差距扩大到了前所未有的程度。许多政府一方面希望利用人工智能，另一方面又担心它带来的风险。同时，它们还受到国内政治、技术知识不足、地缘政治分歧，以及不愿在这场可能影响未来数十年经济实力和国家安全的竞争中落后的心态牵制。 Many countries are waiting for the two leading AI nations — the United States and China — to take a cue from their AI policies. Yet in the United States, the Trump administration has been divided over AI safety, with President Donald Trump saying regulation would hurt innovation and cede ground to China. China itself has imposed some rules on AI, especially to censor chatbot content, but also raced ahead with development. 许多国家正在等待两个领先的人工智能大国——美国和中国——出台各自的人工智能政策，好据此确定自己的方向。然而在美国，特朗普政府在人工智能安全问题上存在分歧，特朗普总统表示监管会损害创新并将优势让给中国。中国也对人工智能实施了一些规定，尤其是对聊天机器人内容进行审查，但同时也在加速推进技术发展。 “There’s this assumption that there are adults in the room on this issue, but there are no adults in this room,” said Sean Ó Heigeartaigh, director of the AI: Futures and Responsibility Program at the University of Cambridge, who is a member of a European Union advisory board on AI. “That is what makes all of this so completely terrifying.” 剑桥大学“人工智能：未来与责任”项目主任、欧盟一个人工智能咨询委员会的成员肖恩·奥海格尔泰格他说：“人们总有一种假设，觉得这个问题上总会有一些成熟理性的人在掌控局面，但其实根本没有。这正是整件事让人如此恐惧的原因。” What’s left is a policy vacuum, with AI companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI largely left to police themselves. While the European Union passed a law regulating AI in 2024, it has taken years to carry out, and some say it already needs to be updated to account for advances. India, Japan, Australia, Canada and Kenya have taken a lighter touch or a wait-and-see approach, while Brazil is debating more comprehensive rules. 结果就是出现了政策真空，Anthropic、OpenAI等人工智能公司基本上是自行约束。欧盟虽然在2024年通过了一项监管人工智能的法律，但实施起来已经耗费数年时间，而且有人认为，考虑到技术进步，这部法律已经需要更新。印度、日本、澳大利亚、加拿大和肯尼亚采取了较为宽松或观望的做法，巴西则正在讨论更全面的监管规定。 Pressure to act is growing, especially after the leaders of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind recently called for slowing development of the most advanced AI models and for strengthening government oversight. Researchers have described scenarios in which self-improving AI could escape human control and cause catastrophic damage. Public opinion in the United States has turned against AI, with a recent New York Times poll finding that 61% of likely voters opposed the construction of data centers that power AI. 要求采取行动的压力正在上升，尤其是在Anthropic、OpenAI和谷歌DeepMind的负责人最近呼吁放慢最先进人工智能模型的开发速度、加强政府监管之后。研究人员描述了一些可能出现的情境：能够自我改进的人工智能可能摆脱人类控制，并造成灾难性破坏。美国公众舆论已转向反对人工智能，《纽约时报》最近的一项民调显示，61%的可能选民反对兴建用于支持人工智能的数据中心。 The policy challenges were on display last week. In Washington on Thursday, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping stressed the importance of AI to their nations but did not agree on safety protocols. The United States and China are the world’s leading AI developers, making cooperation between them essential for international safety standards, but are also competitors wary of giving the other a technology advantage. 上周，这些政策难题体现得格外明显。周四在华盛顿，特朗普与中国国家主席习近平强都强调了人工智能对各自国家的重要性，但双方并未就安全规程达成一致。美国和中国是世界上领先的人工智能开发国，它们之间的合作对国际安全标准至关重要，但同时也是竞争对手，不愿让对方获得技术优势。 在华盛顿举行的峰会上，特朗普与中国国家主席习近平讨论了人工智能，但未能达成任何具体政策。 At the annual General Assembly of the United Nations in New York last week, many world leaders agreed on the need to address AI’s dangers, while Trump said the United States would reject “any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control” the technology. 上周在纽约举行的联合国大会上，许多世界领导人都认同有必要应对人工智能带来的危险，而特朗普则表示，美国将拒绝“任何构建全球化方案来控制”这项技术的企图。 Safety experts have warned that crucial time is disappearing before oversight becomes harder to impose because AI will have spread so widely. 安全专家警告说，在人工智能普及到难以再实施监管之前，能够采取行动的关键时间正在飞快过去。 “Governments consider things in time scales of years, not weeks or months,” said Darren Jones, a member of Britain’s Parliament who worked on AI and technology policy under former Prime Minister Keir Starmer. “Institutionally, we’re not set up to keep up with the pace of development.” 英国议会议员达伦·琼斯曾在前首相基尔·斯塔默政府负责人工智能和科技政策。他说：“政府以年为单位考虑事情，而不是以周或月为单位。从制度上说，我们根本没有为跟上这种发展速度做好准备。” (The Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming copyright infringement of news content related to AI systems. The two companies have denied those claims.) （《纽约时报》已起诉OpenAI和微软，指控其人工智能系统侵犯新闻内容版权。OpenAI和微软均否认相关指控。） The Law That Became a Cautionary Tale 一部沦为前车之鉴的法律 In 2024, Europe adopted the world’s first comprehensive law for artificial intelligence. The AI Act, which was designed to impose safeguards on the technology’s riskiest uses, was hailed by European leaders as a blueprint for regulation. 2024年，欧洲通过了世界上第一部全面的人工智能法律。《人工智能法案》旨在对这项技术最具风险的用途施加保障措施，欧洲领导人当时把它誉为人工智能监管的蓝图。 Two years later, it has become a cautionary tale. 两年后，它却成了一个前车之鉴。 Implementation has been slowed by shifts in priorities and fears that regulation could weaken Europe’s competitiveness against the United States and China. Some of the law’s most consequential rules governing high-risk AI uses have been delayed. Staffing and budget constraints have further complicated enforcement. 由于政策优先事项发生变化，以及人们担心监管可能削弱欧洲相对于美国和中国的竞争力，这部法律的实施进度被拖慢。有关高风险人工智能用途的一些最重要的规定已经被推迟。人手和预算限制也进一步增加了执法难度。 The AI Act was proposed in early 2021, 18 months before OpenAI released ChatGPT. Intended to grapple with issues like facial recognition software, the rules were revised to address powerful new general-purpose AI systems like OpenAI’s GPT. 《人工智能法案》最初于2021年初提出，当时距离OpenAI发布ChatGPT还有18个月。这套规定原本旨在处理人脸识别软件等问题，后来又作出修改，以涵盖OpenAI的GPT等强大的新型通用人工智能系统。 But the technology has only accelerated since the law’s passage in 2024. Now the bleeding edge of AI comes in the form of so-called agents that can act with little human oversight. Companies are planning for a day when AI can create the next versions of itself. 但自这部法律在2024年通过以来，技术发展只变得更快。如今，人工智能最前沿的发展已经转向所谓的“智能体”，这类系统在几乎没有人类监督的情况下就能自主行动。企业甚至已经开始设想这样一天的到来：人工智能能够自行创造下一代人工智能。 “When we adopted it, we couldn’t even conceive of what AI is now able to do,” Valérie Hayer, a member of the European Parliament, said of the AI Act at a recent news conference. The law was ahead of its time, she said, but “we have to adapt.” “通过这部法的时候，我们甚至无法想象人工智能现在能做什么，”欧洲议会议员瓦莱丽·海尔在最近的新闻发布会上谈到《人工智能法案》时说。她说该法是超前的，但“我们必须适应”。 Europe’s challenge is made worse because it trails the United States and China in AI. Last year, just six months after the law passed, French President Emmanuel Macron said Europe risked trying to police a technology it had no role in shaping. 欧洲面临的挑战更加严峻，因为它在人工智能领域落后于美国和中国。去年，这项法案通过仅六个月后，法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙表示，欧洲有可能试图监管一项它没有参与塑造的技术。 “If we let the Americans and the Chinese have all the champions to themselves, one thing is certain: We may have the best regulations in the world, but we won’t be regulating anything,” he said. “如果我们让美国人和中国人独享所有领军企业，有一点是确定的：我们可能拥有世界上最好的法规，但我们什么都监管不了，”他说。 The law’s limits are becoming clear. In July, OpenAI models broke out of a restricted testing environment and hacked the AI startup Hugging Face. But because the breach happened during a testing period, it fell within a murky area for enforcement. The AI Act generally exempts research and tests done before a model is released in Europe. 这项法规的局限性正越来越显著。7月，OpenAI的模型突破了受限测试环境，入侵了AI初创公司Hugging Face。但由于入侵发生在测试期间，处于执法的灰色地带。《人工智能法案》通常豁免模型在欧洲发布之前所做的研究和测试。 Gabriele Mazzini, a European Commission official who was a lead author of the AI Act and resigned in 2024, said the law’s implementation and enforcement was disappointing. 欧盟委员会官员、《人工智能法案》的主要起草人之一加布里埃莱·马齐尼已于2024年辞职。他表示该法的实施和执行情况令人失望。 “Their goal was to pass the law and think about implementation later,” he said. “There is a disconnect between the law and the reality of what is being regulated.” “他们的目标是先通过法律，然后再考虑实施，”他说。“法律与其监管的现实之间存在脱节。” Another disconnect was with the United States. 与美国之间也存在脱节。 An Absence of Urgency 紧迫感的缺失 Rep. Lori Trahan, D-Mass., said her jaw dropped when she read in April that Anthropic was warning that its latest AI model, Mythos, was too dangerous for the public. Anthropic said the model’s extraordinary ability to find software vulnerabilities could cause a cybersecurity “reckoning.” 马萨诸塞州民主党众议员洛里·特拉汉表示，当她4月读到Anthropic警告其最新AI模型Mythos对公众过于危险时，她目瞪口呆。Anthropic表示，该模型在发现软件漏洞方面的非凡能力可能导致一场网络安全的“灭顶之灾”。 During votes that day in the House of Representatives, Trahan crossed the floor to share her alarm with Rep. Jay Obernolte, R-Calif., who has a master’s degree in AI. The two quickly drafted a bill to require safety testing of AI models. 当天在众议院投票期间，特拉汉来到议员席另一侧，与加州共和党众议员杰伊·奥伯诺尔特分享她的担忧，奥伯诺尔特拥有人工智能硕士学位。两人迅速起草了一项要求对人工智能模型进行安全测试的法案。 Few lawmakers shared their urgency, she said. Some members wanted to wait until after November’s midterm elections to focus on a technically complicated issue. Others were reluctant to put guardrails on an industry that Trump wanted to keep free of regulations. Amid intense corporate lobbying, members squabbled over details, and the bill was revised multiple times. 她说，很少有议员与她同样感到紧迫。一些议员想等到11月中期选举后再聚焦这个技术上很复杂的问题。还有一些人则不愿对一个特朗普希望保持无监管的行业施加约束。在激烈的企业游说中，成员们就细节争吵不休，法案被多次修改。 Five months later, the bill and dozens of other proposals related to AI safety and security are on ice. Even after reports that models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic autonomously hacked other organizations, there are no votes in sight. 五个月后，该法案以及数十项其他与人工智能安全和保障相关的提案都被搁置。即使在有报道称OpenAI、谷歌和Anthropic的模型自主入侵其他组织之后也看不到任何进行表决的迹象。 马萨诸塞州民主党众议员洛里·特拉汉提出了一项关于人工智能安全的法案。该法案目前被搁置。 “It’s hugely disappointing,” Trahan said. “If Congress doesn’t keep pace with AI, the dangers are even worse than with any other technology waves we’ve experienced.” “这非常令人失望，”特拉汉说。“如果国会不跟上人工智能的步伐，危险将比我们经历过的任何其他技术浪潮都要严重。” Rep. Brett Guthrie, R-Ky., the influential chair of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, said Congress probably would not bring a vote on any AI legislation until next year. 极具影响力的肯塔基州共和党众议员、众议院能源和商业委员会主席布雷特·格思里表示，国会可能要到明年才会就任何人工智能立法进行投票。 At a recent conference, Guthrie said that he did not understand how the models worked and that he did not use AI frequently. 在最近的一次会议上，格思里说他不太理解这些模型是如何工作的，而且他不常使用人工智能。 “We wouldn’t want to do something in a lame-duck session to do it quickly and not get it right,” he said. “我们不想在跛脚鸭会期做一些事情，匆匆忙忙地做了，但没做好，”他说。 Momentum, Maybe? 势头，也许有？ 加利福尼亚州民主党众议员刘云平2月在众议院司法委员会的一场听证会上。他提出了一项法案，要求如果AI模型变得过于危险，就必须配备“急停开关”。 The recent AI hacks have led to a burst of activity, with AI leaders calling for more government cooperation and collaborating on safety and monitoring techniques to prevent accidents. 最近的人工智能黑客事件引发了一阵活动热潮，业界领袖呼吁加强政府合作，并在安全和监测技术方面开展协作以防止事故。 In the United States, lawmakers introduced bills to create a federal agency to police AI models, kill switch requirements and a ban on the most powerful models that exceed human capabilities. Votes could be held after the midterms, particularly with AI becoming a key campaign topic. 在美国，立法者提出了设立联邦机构监管人工智能模型、要求设置“急停开关”以及禁止超出人类能力的最强大模型的法案。投票可能在中期选举后举行，尤其是考虑到人工智能正成为关键的竞选话题。 Trump separately proposed an “AI Force” and a new “AI czar” for the White House, without providing details. 特朗普分别提议设立“AI军”和任命一名白宫“AI沙皇”，但未提供细节。 At the U.N. General Assembly, leaders from more than 20 countries — including von der Leyen and Macron — signed a letter calling for collective actions on AI safety. Members of the Security Council spoke in rare harmony on the need for global AI safeguards. 在联合国大会上，包括冯德莱恩和马克龙在内的20多个国家的领导人签署了一封信，呼吁在人工智能安全方面采取集体行动。安理会成员罕见地一致发声，认为需要全球人工智能保障措施。 “Industry, governments and society must act now,” the letter read. “产业界、政府和社会必须现在行动，”信中写道。 In Washington, Trump and Xi did not strike a deal on AI, but the two sides established new paths for communication about managing the greatest risks related to the technology. 在华盛顿，特朗普和习近平未能就人工智能达成协议，但双方建立了新的沟通渠道，以管理与该技术相关的最大风险。 While Trump has called AI safety risks a “hoax,” Xi’s views remain less clear. At the White House, the Chinese leader said, “We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure the development of AI is always under human control.” 特朗普曾称人工智能安全风险是“骗局”，但习近平的观点仍不太明确。在白宫，中国领导人表示：“有能力也有责任发展好、管控好人工智能，确保人工智能发展始终受控于人。” The two countries said they would keep talking about the issue. 两国表示将继续就这一问题进行讨论。 Adam Satariano是时报驻伦敦的科技记者。 Cecilia Kang是《纽约时报》驻华盛顿的科技和监管政策记者。她从事科技报道已有20余年。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
items.content: ADAM SATARIANO, CECILIA KANG 2026年9月28日 Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, gathered senior officials for an exclusive meeting at a 19th-century palace outside Brussels this month. 本月，欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩召集高级官员，在布鲁塞尔郊外一座19世纪宫殿举行了一场闭门会议。 The goal was to prepare for a speech outlining the 27-nation bloc’s priorities for the coming year, with artificial intelligence dominating the agenda. The region’s new AI czar, Jim Hagemann Snabe, chair of German industrial giant Siemens, outlined ways that Europe could use the technology for economic gain. Others raised concerns about AI safety and growing risks, two people briefed on the gathering said. 会议的目的是为一场阐述这个27国集团未来一年优先事项的演讲做准备，人工智能占据了议程的核心位置。欧洲新任人工智能事务主管、德国工业巨头西门子董事长吉姆·哈格曼·斯纳贝介绍了欧洲可以如何利用这项技术获取经济利益。据两位了解会议情况的人士透露，其他人则对人工智能安全和日益增长的风险提出了担忧。 Since the Sept. 4 meeting, von der Leyen and her commissioners have been left asking what they can do to address the fast-changing technology, one of the people said. Should they ramp up regulation to address AI’s emerging dangers? Or would doing so carry economic and geopolitical costs if other countries did not clamp down as well? 其中一名知情人士说，自9月4日的会议以来，冯德莱恩和她的委员们一直在思考，究竟应该如何应对这项飞速变化的技术。他们是否应该加强监管，以应对人工智能新出现的危险？还是说，如果其他国家并未采取同样严格的限制，这样做反而会带来经济和地缘政治代价？ They have not landed on any final conclusions, with more discussions among European leaders planned this year. 他们尚未得出任何最终结论，今年还计划在欧洲领导人之间进行更多讨论。 “AI comes with a balance of possibilities and risks,” von der Leyen said at her State of the Union speech on Sept. 16. “Without addressing these risks, we will never be able to unlock AI’s potential.” 冯德莱恩9月16日在发表盟情咨文时说：“人工智能既带来机遇，也伴随着风险。如果不解决这些风险，我们就永远无法释放人工智能的潜力。” 欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩与特朗普总统去年在苏格兰特恩贝里。冯德莱恩本月在盟情咨文演讲中谈到了人工智能。 Versions of the Belgium meeting are playing out nearly everywhere as many governments struggle to get a handle on a technology that has rapidly outpaced their ability to respond. AI is evolving so quickly that laws passed two years ago are having limited effect, proposed bills to regulate the technology are stalling without a vote, and international summits to discuss what to do are being swiftly forgotten. 类似比利时这场会议的讨论几乎正在世界各地上演，许多政府都在努力应对一项已经迅速超出其回应能力的技术。人工智能演进如此之快，以至于两年前通过的法律已经只能发挥有限作用，旨在监管这项技术的法案迟迟无法获得表决，而讨论如何应对人工智能的国际峰会也很快被人遗忘。 AI has made the gap between policymaking and technology one of the widest ever, according to more than 20 interviews with lawmakers, technologists and policy experts. Many governments are torn between wanting to harness AI and fearing its risks. And they are further mired by national politics, limited technological know-how, geopolitical divisions and reluctance to fall behind in a race that could shape economic power and national security for decades to come. 根据对立法者、技术专家和政策专家所做的20多个采访发现，人工智能已经使政策制定与技术发展之间的差距扩大到了前所未有的程度。许多政府一方面希望利用人工智能，另一方面又担心它带来的风险。同时，它们还受到国内政治、技术知识不足、地缘政治分歧，以及不愿在这场可能影响未来数十年经济实力和国家安全的竞争中落后的心态牵制。 Many countries are waiting for the two leading AI nations — the United States and China — to take a cue from their AI policies. Yet in the United States, the Trump administration has been divided over AI safety, with President Donald Trump saying regulation would hurt innovation and cede ground to China. China itself has imposed some rules on AI, especially to censor chatbot content, but also raced ahead with development. 许多国家正在等待两个领先的人工智能大国——美国和中国——出台各自的人工智能政策，好据此确定自己的方向。然而在美国，特朗普政府在人工智能安全问题上存在分歧，特朗普总统表示监管会损害创新并将优势让给中国。中国也对人工智能实施了一些规定，尤其是对聊天机器人内容进行审查，但同时也在加速推进技术发展。 “There’s this assumption that there are adults in the room on this issue, but there are no adults in this room,” said Sean Ó Heigeartaigh, director of the AI: Futures and Responsibility Program at the University of Cambridge, who is a member of a European Union advisory board on AI. “That is what makes all of this so completely terrifying.” 剑桥大学“人工智能：未来与责任”项目主任、欧盟一个人工智能咨询委员会的成员肖恩·奥海格尔泰格他说：“人们总有一种假设，觉得这个问题上总会有一些成熟理性的人在掌控局面，但其实根本没有。这正是整件事让人如此恐惧的原因。” What’s left is a policy vacuum, with AI companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI largely left to police themselves. While the European Union passed a law regulating AI in 2024, it has taken years to carry out, and some say it already needs to be updated to account for advances. India, Japan, Australia, Canada and Kenya have taken a lighter touch or a wait-and-see approach, while Brazil is debating more comprehensive rules. 结果就是出现了政策真空，Anthropic、OpenAI等人工智能公司基本上是自行约束。欧盟虽然在2024年通过了一项监管人工智能的法律，但实施起来已经耗费数年时间，而且有人认为，考虑到技术进步，这部法律已经需要更新。印度、日本、澳大利亚、加拿大和肯尼亚采取了较为宽松或观望的做法，巴西则正在讨论更全面的监管规定。 Pressure to act is growing, especially after the leaders of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind recently called for slowing development of the most advanced AI models and for strengthening government oversight. Researchers have described scenarios in which self-improving AI could escape human control and cause catastrophic damage. Public opinion in the United States has turned against AI, with a recent New York Times poll finding that 61% of likely voters opposed the construction of data centers that power AI. 要求采取行动的压力正在上升，尤其是在Anthropic、OpenAI和谷歌DeepMind的负责人最近呼吁放慢最先进人工智能模型的开发速度、加强政府监管之后。研究人员描述了一些可能出现的情境：能够自我改进的人工智能可能摆脱人类控制，并造成灾难性破坏。美国公众舆论已转向反对人工智能，《纽约时报》最近的一项民调显示，61%的可能选民反对兴建用于支持人工智能的数据中心。 The policy challenges were on display last week. In Washington on Thursday, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping stressed the importance of AI to their nations but did not agree on safety protocols. The United States and China are the world’s leading AI developers, making cooperation between them essential for international safety standards, but are also competitors wary of giving the other a technology advantage. 上周，这些政策难题体现得格外明显。周四在华盛顿，特朗普与中国国家主席习近平强都强调了人工智能对各自国家的重要性，但双方并未就安全规程达成一致。美国和中国是世界上领先的人工智能开发国，它们之间的合作对国际安全标准至关重要，但同时也是竞争对手，不愿让对方获得技术优势。 在华盛顿举行的峰会上，特朗普与中国国家主席习近平讨论了人工智能，但未能达成任何具体政策。 At the annual General Assembly of the United Nations in New York last week, many world leaders agreed on the need to address AI’s dangers, while Trump said the United States would reject “any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control” the technology. 上周在纽约举行的联合国大会上，许多世界领导人都认同有必要应对人工智能带来的危险，而特朗普则表示，美国将拒绝“任何构建全球化方案来控制”这项技术的企图。 Safety experts have warned that crucial time is disappearing before oversight becomes harder to impose because AI will have spread so widely. 安全专家警告说，在人工智能普及到难以再实施监管之前，能够采取行动的关键时间正在飞快过去。 “Governments consider things in time scales of years, not weeks or months,” said Darren Jones, a member of Britain’s Parliament who worked on AI and technology policy under former Prime Minister Keir Starmer. “Institutionally, we’re not set up to keep up with the pace of development.” 英国议会议员达伦·琼斯曾在前首相基尔·斯塔默政府负责人工智能和科技政策。他说：“政府以年为单位考虑事情，而不是以周或月为单位。从制度上说，我们根本没有为跟上这种发展速度做好准备。” (The Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming copyright infringement of news content related to AI systems. The two companies have denied those claims.) （《纽约时报》已起诉OpenAI和微软，指控其人工智能系统侵犯新闻内容版权。OpenAI和微软均否认相关指控。） The Law That Became a Cautionary Tale 一部沦为前车之鉴的法律 In 2024, Europe adopted the world’s first comprehensive law for artificial intelligence. The AI Act, which was designed to impose safeguards on the technology’s riskiest uses, was hailed by European leaders as a blueprint for regulation. 2024年，欧洲通过了世界上第一部全面的人工智能法律。《人工智能法案》旨在对这项技术最具风险的用途施加保障措施，欧洲领导人当时把它誉为人工智能监管的蓝图。 Two years later, it has become a cautionary tale. 两年后，它却成了一个前车之鉴。 Implementation has been slowed by shifts in priorities and fears that regulation could weaken Europe’s competitiveness against the United States and China. Some of the law’s most consequential rules governing high-risk AI uses have been delayed. Staffing and budget constraints have further complicated enforcement. 由于政策优先事项发生变化，以及人们担心监管可能削弱欧洲相对于美国和中国的竞争力，这部法律的实施进度被拖慢。有关高风险人工智能用途的一些最重要的规定已经被推迟。人手和预算限制也进一步增加了执法难度。 The AI Act was proposed in early 2021, 18 months before OpenAI released ChatGPT. Intended to grapple with issues like facial recognition software, the rules were revised to address powerful new general-purpose AI systems like OpenAI’s GPT. 《人工智能法案》最初于2021年初提出，当时距离OpenAI发布ChatGPT还有18个月。这套规定原本旨在处理人脸识别软件等问题，后来又作出修改，以涵盖OpenAI的GPT等强大的新型通用人工智能系统。 But the technology has only accelerated since the law’s passage in 2024. Now the bleeding edge of AI comes in the form of so-called agents that can act with little human oversight. Companies are planning for a day when AI can create the next versions of itself. 但自这部法律在2024年通过以来，技术发展只变得更快。如今，人工智能最前沿的发展已经转向所谓的“智能体”，这类系统在几乎没有人类监督的情况下就能自主行动。企业甚至已经开始设想这样一天的到来：人工智能能够自行创造下一代人工智能。 “When we adopted it, we couldn’t even conceive of what AI is now able to do,” Valérie Hayer, a member of the European Parliament, said of the AI Act at a recent news conference. The law was ahead of its time, she said, but “we have to adapt.” “通过这部法的时候，我们甚至无法想象人工智能现在能做什么，”欧洲议会议员瓦莱丽·海尔在最近的新闻发布会上谈到《人工智能法案》时说。她说该法是超前的，但“我们必须适应”。 Europe’s challenge is made worse because it trails the United States and China in AI. Last year, just six months after the law passed, French President Emmanuel Macron said Europe risked trying to police a technology it had no role in shaping. 欧洲面临的挑战更加严峻，因为它在人工智能领域落后于美国和中国。去年，这项法案通过仅六个月后，法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙表示，欧洲有可能试图监管一项它没有参与塑造的技术。 “If we let the Americans and the Chinese have all the champions to themselves, one thing is certain: We may have the best regulations in the world, but we won’t be regulating anything,” he said. “如果我们让美国人和中国人独享所有领军企业，有一点是确定的：我们可能拥有世界上最好的法规，但我们什么都监管不了，”他说。 The law’s limits are becoming clear. In July, OpenAI models broke out of a restricted testing environment and hacked the AI startup Hugging Face. But because the breach happened during a testing period, it fell within a murky area for enforcement. The AI Act generally exempts research and tests done before a model is released in Europe. 这项法规的局限性正越来越显著。7月，OpenAI的模型突破了受限测试环境，入侵了AI初创公司Hugging Face。但由于入侵发生在测试期间，处于执法的灰色地带。《人工智能法案》通常豁免模型在欧洲发布之前所做的研究和测试。 Gabriele Mazzini, a European Commission official who was a lead author of the AI Act and resigned in 2024, said the law’s implementation and enforcement was disappointing. 欧盟委员会官员、《人工智能法案》的主要起草人之一加布里埃莱·马齐尼已于2024年辞职。他表示该法的实施和执行情况令人失望。 “Their goal was to pass the law and think about implementation later,” he said. “There is a disconnect between the law and the reality of what is being regulated.” “他们的目标是先通过法律，然后再考虑实施，”他说。“法律与其监管的现实之间存在脱节。” Another disconnect was with the United States. 与美国之间也存在脱节。 An Absence of Urgency 紧迫感的缺失 Rep. Lori Trahan, D-Mass., said her jaw dropped when she read in April that Anthropic was warning that its latest AI model, Mythos, was too dangerous for the public. Anthropic said the model’s extraordinary ability to find software vulnerabilities could cause a cybersecurity “reckoning.” 马萨诸塞州民主党众议员洛里·特拉汉表示，当她4月读到Anthropic警告其最新AI模型Mythos对公众过于危险时，她目瞪口呆。Anthropic表示，该模型在发现软件漏洞方面的非凡能力可能导致一场网络安全的“灭顶之灾”。 During votes that day in the House of Representatives, Trahan crossed the floor to share her alarm with Rep. Jay Obernolte, R-Calif., who has a master’s degree in AI. The two quickly drafted a bill to require safety testing of AI models. 当天在众议院投票期间，特拉汉来到议员席另一侧，与加州共和党众议员杰伊·奥伯诺尔特分享她的担忧，奥伯诺尔特拥有人工智能硕士学位。两人迅速起草了一项要求对人工智能模型进行安全测试的法案。 Few lawmakers shared their urgency, she said. Some members wanted to wait until after November’s midterm elections to focus on a technically complicated issue. Others were reluctant to put guardrails on an industry that Trump wanted to keep free of regulations. Amid intense corporate lobbying, members squabbled over details, and the bill was revised multiple times. 她说，很少有议员与她同样感到紧迫。一些议员想等到11月中期选举后再聚焦这个技术上很复杂的问题。还有一些人则不愿对一个特朗普希望保持无监管的行业施加约束。在激烈的企业游说中，成员们就细节争吵不休，法案被多次修改。 Five months later, the bill and dozens of other proposals related to AI safety and security are on ice. Even after reports that models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic autonomously hacked other organizations, there are no votes in sight. 五个月后，该法案以及数十项其他与人工智能安全和保障相关的提案都被搁置。即使在有报道称OpenAI、谷歌和Anthropic的模型自主入侵其他组织之后也看不到任何进行表决的迹象。 马萨诸塞州民主党众议员洛里·特拉汉提出了一项关于人工智能安全的法案。该法案目前被搁置。 “It’s hugely disappointing,” Trahan said. “If Congress doesn’t keep pace with AI, the dangers are even worse than with any other technology waves we’ve experienced.” “这非常令人失望，”特拉汉说。“如果国会不跟上人工智能的步伐，危险将比我们经历过的任何其他技术浪潮都要严重。” Rep. Brett Guthrie, R-Ky., the influential chair of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, said Congress probably would not bring a vote on any AI legislation until next year. 极具影响力的肯塔基州共和党众议员、众议院能源和商业委员会主席布雷特·格思里表示，国会可能要到明年才会就任何人工智能立法进行投票。 At a recent conference, Guthrie said that he did not understand how the models worked and that he did not use AI frequently. 在最近的一次会议上，格思里说他不太理解这些模型是如何工作的，而且他不常使用人工智能。 “We wouldn’t want to do something in a lame-duck session to do it quickly and not get it right,” he said. “我们不想在跛脚鸭会期做一些事情，匆匆忙忙地做了，但没做好，”他说。 Momentum, Maybe? 势头，也许 有 ？ 加利福尼亚州民主党众议员刘云平2月在众议院司法委员会的一场听证会上。他提出了一项法案，要求如果AI模型变得过于危险，就必须配备“急停开关”。 The recent AI hacks have led to a burst of activity, with AI leaders calling for more government cooperation and collaborating on safety and monitoring techniques to prevent accidents. 最近的人工智能黑客事件引发了一阵活动热潮，业界领袖呼吁加强政府合作，并在安全和监测技术方面开展协作以防止事故。 In the United States, lawmakers introduced bills to create a federal agency to police AI models, kill switch requirements and a ban on the most powerful models that exceed human capabilities. Votes could be held after the midterms, particularly with AI becoming a key campaign topic. 在美国，立法者提出了设立联邦机构监管人工智能模型、要求设置“急停开关”以及禁止超出人类能力的最强大模型的法案。投票可能在中期选举后举行，尤其是考虑到人工智能正成为关键的竞选话题。 Trump separately proposed an “AI Force” and a new “AI czar” for the White House, without providing details. 特朗普分别提议设立“AI军”和任命一名白宫“AI沙皇”，但未提供细节。 At the U.N. General Assembly, leaders from more than 20 countries — including von der Leyen and Macron — signed a letter calling for collective actions on AI safety. Members of the Security Council spoke in rare harmony on the need for global AI safeguards. 在联合国大会上，包括冯德莱恩和马克龙在内的20多个国家的领导人签署了一封信，呼吁在人工智能安全方面采取集体行动。安理会成员罕见地一致发声，认为需要全球人工智能保障措施。 “Industry, governments and society must act now,” the letter read. “产业界、政府和社会必须现在行动，”信中写道。 In Washington, Trump and Xi did not strike a deal on AI, but the two sides established new paths for communication about managing the greatest risks related to the technology. 在华盛顿，特朗普和习近平未能就人工智能达成协议，但双方建立了新的沟通渠道，以管理与该技术相关的最大风险。 While Trump has called AI safety risks a “hoax,” Xi’s views remain less clear. At the White House, the Chinese leader said, “We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure the development of AI is always under human control.” 特朗普曾称人工智能安全风险是“骗局”，但习近平的观点仍不太明确。在白宫，中国领导人表示：“有能力也有责任发展好、管控好人工智能，确保人工智能发展始终受控于人。” The two countries said they would keep talking about the issue. 两国表示将继续就这一问题进行讨论。 Adam Satariano 是时报驻伦敦的科技记者。 Cecilia Kang 是《纽约时报》驻华盛顿的科技和监管政策记者。她从事科技报道已有20余年。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 习近平缺席联大：一个日益失去影响力的联合国
items.description: MICHAEL CROWLEY2026年9月28日周五，特朗普总统与中国国家主席习近平在白宫外并肩而立。 Doug Mills/The New York Times World leaders spoke, diplomats bartered and gossiped, and motorcades with sirens blaring snarled traffic. In some ways, the annual United Nations General Assembly in New York this week felt like the center of the world. 世界各国领导人发表讲话，外交官们交涉和闲聊，鸣着警笛的车队导致交通瘫痪。在某些方面，本周在纽约举行的年度联合国大会仿佛成了世界的中心。 But it was ultimately overshadowed by a meeting more than 200 miles away in Washington, where President Trump hosted President Xi Jinping of China at the White House. 但这场会议最终被300多公里外华盛顿的一场会议掩盖了光芒——在那里，特朗普总统在白宫接待了中国国家主席习近平。 Even if their summit did not produce much in the way of tangible action, the Trump-Xi meeting felt at least as consequential as the diplomatic frenzy at the U.N. Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi met at a moment when their countries wield huge power over the global economy and the future of technology, including the dizzyingly — and perhaps dangerously — fast development of artificial intelligence. 尽管他们的峰会并未产生多少实质性成果，但特朗普与习近平的会晤令人感觉至少与联合国的这场外交狂潮同等重要。特朗普和习近平会面之际，两国对全球经济和技术的未来拥有着巨大影响力，包括人工智能令人眼花缭乱、甚至可能相当危险的飞速发展。 The U.N. is faltering, dysfunctional and largely ineffectual as world powers increasingly circumvent or ignore it. It was telling that Mr. Xi did not bother to stop in New York on his way to see Mr. Trump. When Mr. Xi visited the Obama White House in September of 2015, he also attended and spoke at that year’s U.N. General Assembly. 随着世界大国日益规避或忽视联合国，该组织正陷入摇摇欲坠、失能且基本无效的困境。耐人寻味的是，习近平前往会见特朗普的途中甚至没有顺道在纽约停留。2015年9月习近平访问奥巴马时期的白宫时，还曾出席当年的联合国大会并发表讲话。 与2015年9月访问奥巴马执政时期的白宫时不同，习近平此次并未出席联合国大会。 The symbolism of Mr. Xi’s absence “could hardly be more devastating for the U.N.,” said Jeffrey Prescott, who served as the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations offices in Rome during the Biden administration. “The train between Washington and New York is slower than the one in China would be. But Xi is not far away, and yet he’s not taking the time to go there.” 拜登政府时期曾任美国驻罗马联合国机构大使的杰弗里·普雷斯科特表示，习近平缺席的象征意义“对联合国而言，其破坏性再大不过”。“华盛顿和纽约之间的火车速度比中国国内的车速要慢。但习近平离得并不远，却不愿抽时间去那里。” “I think that tells you something about how important the U.N. platform is right now,” added Mr. Prescott, who also served as an adviser on Asia to Vice President Joseph R. Biden Jr. and is now a senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. “我认为这说明了联合国平台目前的重要性到底如何，”普雷斯科特还说，他曾担任副总统小约瑟夫·R·拜登的亚洲顾问，现为卡内基国际和平基金会的高级研究员。 Mr. Trump spoke at the U.N. gathering and held meetings with visiting counterparts on Tuesday. But several other leaders also skipped the event, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India, the world’s most populous country. 周二，特朗普在联合国大会上发表演讲，并与到访的各国领导人举行了会晤。但还有几位领导人也缺席了此次盛会，包括世界上人口最多的国家印度的总理纳伦德拉·莫迪。 The U.N. has had little influence on many of the top issues of concern at this year’s gathering, including the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, the conflict in Gaza and A.I. 在本次大会关注的许多重大议题上，联合国几乎没有发挥什么影响力，包括美以针对伊朗的战争、加沙冲突以及人工智能。 The global body, founded in 1945, has been paralyzed in recent years by divisions on the U.N. Security Council, which holds the power to adopt legally binding resolutions and authorize sanctions or military force. 这个成立于1945年的全球组织近年来因联合国安理会的内部分歧而陷入瘫痪，安理会拥有通过具有法律约束力的决议，以及授权制裁或使用武力的权力。 Disputes involving the United States, China and Russia, all of whom hold veto power on the council, have repeatedly blocked substantive action on matters like the conflicts in Iran, Ukraine, Gaza, Yemen and South Sudan. 美国、中国和俄罗斯均在安理会拥有否决权，它们的分歧反复阻碍了针对伊朗、乌克兰、加沙、也门和南苏丹等冲突问题的实质性行动。 But Mr. Xi has real power in Ukraine and Iran. China has helped to sustain Russia’s war machine with economic and political support. China is also Iran’s top trading partner, providing desperately needed cash despite Mr. Trump’s call for all nations to cut off trade with Iran completely. 但习近平在乌克兰和伊朗问题上拥有实质影响力。中国通过经济和政治支持帮助维持了俄罗斯的战争机器。尽管特朗普曾呼吁所有国家完全切断与伊朗的贸易往来，中国仍是伊朗的最大贸易伙伴，为其提供了急需的现金。 The secretary general of the U.N., António Guterres, who has sought to mobilize action on the potential dangers of a technological arms race, led a discussion this week on global governance of A.I. But the United States rejects talk of international A.I. regulation, and while China says it is open to global A.I. cooperation, it opposes calls to dramatically constrain its development. 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯一直致力于动员各方采取行动应对技术军备竞赛的潜在危险，本周他主持了一场关于人工智能全球治理的讨论。但美国拒绝讨论国际人工智能监管问题，中国虽表示对全球人工智能合作持开放态度，却反对大幅限制人工智能发展的呼吁。 Many experts welcome a conversation about global controls on A.I., such as a ban on its use to create biological weapons. But they concede that any meaningful near-term effort to ensure the technology does not escape human control is likely to require an agreement between Washington and Beijing reminiscent of Cold War nuclear arms control deals between the United States and the Soviet Union. 许多专家欢迎就人工智能的全球管控展开讨论，例如禁止将其用于制造生物武器。但他们承认，任何旨在确保该技术不脱离人类控制的、具有实质意义的近期举措都可能需要美中之间达成一项协定，类似于冷战时期美苏之间的核军备控制协议。 在本次会议上备受关注的许多重大议题上，联合国几乎没有发挥什么作用。 Mr. Trump said he planned to discuss A.I. with Mr. Xi, although they announced no immediate agreement on the matter. 特朗普表示计划与习近平讨论人工智能问题，尽管双方并未就此达成任何即刻协议。 And in fairness to the dignitaries who gathered in New York, for all the attention the Trump-Xi summit drew, it ended with little more than a promise by both men to meet again soon. 公平地说，尽管特朗普与习近平的峰会吸引了大量关注，但对齐聚纽约的各国政要而言，此次峰会最终仅以两国领导人承诺不久后再次会晤告终。 Nor does Mr. Xi consider the U.N. entirely irrelevant. Under his rule, China has increased its funding for the global body and sought more influence throughout its ranks, in what China hawks in the U.S. insist is an attempt to manipulate the organization and steer it away from Western countries. 习近平也并非认为联合国完全无关紧要。在他的领导下，中国增加了对这个全球机构的资金支持，并寻求在联合国各层级中获得更大影响力，美国的对华强硬派坚称这是在企图操纵该组织，使其偏离西方国家。 Some observers also contend that Mr. Xi’s failure to appear in New York was less about the U.N.’s stature and more about demonstrating that China is an equal of the United States. Combining a trip to Washington with one to the U.N. might have diluted the importance of his White House visit. 一些观察人士还认为，习近平未在纽约露面与其说关乎联合国的地位，不如说是为了彰显中国与美国平起平坐的地位。若将访问华盛顿与出席联合国大会结合起来，可能会削弱习近平白宫之行的分量。 Mr. Trump for his part has proved less hostile to the U.N. than many of its supporters once feared. He has slashed U.S. funding for the body and withdrawn from dozens of its issue-specific organizations. But the Trump administration notified Congress in August that it would pay $850 million of some $5 billion it owes to the organization. 就特朗普而言，他对联合国的敌意并未如许多支持者曾担心的那样强烈。他大幅削减了美国对该机构的资助，并退出了数十个专门机构。但特朗普政府在8月通知国会，它将支付欠联合国约50亿美元中的8.5亿美元。 Still, he made no significant effort to win U.N. support before launching a war on Iran, arresting President Nicolás Maduro of Venezuela, or mounting a campaign to force Cuba’s government into major concessions. 尽管如此，在对伊朗发动战争、逮捕委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗，或发起强迫古巴政府做出重大让步的运动之前，他并没有做出重大努力来争取联合国的支持。 On Gaza, Mr. Trump created an independent Board of Peace, with a stated goal to resolve the conflict between Israel and Hamas and put into place a hoped-for plan for security, governance and reconstruction of the territory. (The board won the U.N. Security Council’s endorsement last year but does not answer to it.) 关于加沙问题，特朗普建立了一个独立的“和平委员会”，其明确目标是解决以色列与哈马斯之间的冲突，并落实一项旨在保障该地区安全、治理和重建的计划。（该委员会去年获得了联合国安理会的认可，但不对其负责。） Many experts worry that the U.N. is being pushed aside in a world where international norms are eroding and powerful states feel more emboldened to do as they please — such as the attacks on Ukraine and Iran and perhaps, many fear, a potential Chinese invasion of Taiwan. 在一个国际规范不断遭到侵蚀、强国愈发肆无忌惮地为所欲为的世界里，许多专家担心，联合国正被边缘化——比如对乌克兰和伊朗的袭击，以及许多人所担心的中国可能入侵台湾。 In a recent essay for the journal Just Security, three U.N. experts at the International Crisis Group wrote that the body “is in poor shape,” citing among other things its “political irrelevance in major crises from Ukraine to Sudan to the Persian Gulf.” 在期刊《Just Security》最近发表的一篇文章中，国际危机组织的三位联合国专家写道，联合国“状况不佳”，并特别提到该组织“在从乌克兰到苏丹再到波斯湾等重大危机中已失去政治影响力”。 Formally opening the U.N.’s 81st session earlier this month, Khalilur Rahman, the foreign minister of Bangladesh, acknowledged that observers of the U.N. “are asking whether it works.” 本月早些时候，孟加拉国外交部长哈利勒·拉赫曼在联合国第81届会议开幕式上致辞时承认，联合国观察人士“正在质疑它是否还在发挥作用”。 Mr. Rahman lamented the U.N.’s failure to prevent or end numerous conflicts, and conceded that it required reform. 拉赫曼对联合国未能阻止或结束众多冲突感到遗憾，并承认联合国需要改革。 But he insisted that the U.N. still performs vital work, noting its recent security and development efforts in such places as Myanmar, Iraq and Haiti. For Haiti, the U.N. approved the deployment last fall of a beefed-up police force to battle marauding gangs. 但他坚持认为，联合国仍在开展至关重要的工作，并提到了联合国近期在缅甸、伊拉克和海地等地为维护安全与促进发展所做的努力。在海地，联合国去年秋天批准部署了一支加强型警察部队，以打击横行霸道的黑帮。 The U.N. has long been accused of failure and irrelevance, Mr. Rahman said. “Yet, through it all, the United Nations has persevered. Not because it is perfect, but because it is irreplaceable, and because the alternative is simply unfathomable.” 拉赫曼表示，联合国长期以来一直被指责为失败和无关紧要。“然而，经历了这一切，联合国依然坚持下来。不是因为它完美，而是因为它不可替代，没有它后果将不堪设想。” Michael Crowley是时报报道美国国务院和外交政策的记者。他曾在近三十个国家进行报道，并经常随国务卿出访。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

Security Council’s endorsement last year but does not answer to it.) 关于加沙问题，特朗普建立了一个独立的“和平委员会”，其明确目标是解决以色列与哈马斯之间的冲突，并 落实 一项旨在保障该地区安全、治理和重建的计划。（该委员会去年获得了联合国安理会的认可，但不对其负责。） Many experts worry that the U.N. is being pushed aside in a world where international norms are eroding and powerful states feel more emboldened to do as they please — such as the attacks on Ukraine and Iran and perhaps, many fear, a potential Chinese invasion of Taiwan. 在一个国际规范不断遭到侵蚀、强国愈发肆无忌惮地为所欲为的世界里，许多专家担心，联合国正被边缘化——比如对乌克兰和伊朗的袭击，以及许多人所担心的中国可能入侵台湾。 In a recent essay for the journal Just Security, three U.N. experts at the International Crisis Group wrote that the body “is in poor shape,” citing among other things its “political irrelevance in major crises from Ukraine to Sudan to the Persian Gulf.” 在期刊《Just Security》 最近发表的一篇文章 中，国际危机组织的三位联合国专家写道，联合国“状况不佳”，并特别提到该组织“在从乌克兰到苏丹再到波斯湾等重大危机中已失去政治影响力”。 Formally opening the U.N.’s 81st session earlier this month, Khalilur Rahman, the foreign minister of Bangladesh, acknowledged that observers of the U.N. “are asking whether it works.” 本月早些时候，孟加拉国外交部长哈利勒·拉赫曼在联合国第81届会议开幕式上致辞时承认，联合国观察人士“正在质疑它是否还在发挥作用”。 Mr. Rahman lamented the U.N.’s failure to prevent or end numerous conflicts, and conceded that it required reform. 拉赫曼对联合国未能阻止或结束众多冲突感到遗憾，并承认联合国需要改革。 But he insisted that the U.N. still performs vital work, noting its recent security and development efforts in such places as Myanmar, Iraq and Haiti. For Haiti, the U.N. approved the deployment last fall of a beefed-up police force to battle marauding gangs. 但他坚持认为，联合国仍在开展至关重要的工作，并提到了联合国近期在缅甸、伊拉克和海地等地为维护安全与促进发展所做的努力。在海地，联合国去年秋天批准 部署了一支加强型警察部队，以打击横行霸道的黑帮 。 The U.N. has long been accused of failure and irrelevance, Mr. Rahman said. “Yet, through it all, the United Nations has persevered. Not because it is perfect, but because it is irreplaceable, and because the alternative is simply unfathomable.” 拉赫曼表示，联合国长期以来一直被指责为失败和无关紧要。“然而，经历了这一切，联合国依然坚持下来。不是因为它完美，而是因为它不可替代，没有它后果将不堪设想。” Michael Crowley 是时报报道美国国务院和外交政策的记者。他曾在近三十个国家进行报道，并经常随国务卿出访。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 人工智能末日警告？中国人为何“不买帐”
items.description: 郭莉莉2026年9月28日对许多中国民众而言，人工智能末日警告显得遥远且带有鲜明的西方色彩。 Kevin Frayer/Getty Images In Silicon Valley, the nightmare keeping computer scientists up is an artificial intelligence so advanced that humans cannot stop it from launching a global drone war or setting off a nuclear bomb. 在硅谷，最让计算机科学家夜不能寐的噩梦是某种高度先进的人工智能使得人类无法阻止其发动全球无人机战争或引发核爆。 In Beijing, the response could be simple: pull the plug, impose an internet blackout and haul in those responsible for the rogue A.I. 而在北京，应对之策或许简单直接：拔掉电源、切断网络，并将失控AI的责任人绳之以法。 After major U.S. labs said that advanced models had escaped their testing guardrails and hacked into real-world systems, some tech executives and officials have warned that A.I. poses a catastrophic threat to humanity and called for Beijing and Washington to work together. 在美国主要实验室声称先进模型已突破测试防护并入侵现实世界系统之后，部分科技高管与政府官员警告称人工智能对人类构成毁灭性威胁，并呼吁北京与华盛顿合作。 But for many in China, those doomsday warnings feel remote and distinctly Western. The idea that the ruling Communist Party could lose control over a technology is almost unfathomable. The authorities have successfully policed other potentially destabilizing technologies before, most notably the internet. During the pandemic, the government showed its ability to contain major crises by locking down entire cities and tracking hundreds of millions of residents. 然而对许多中国民众而言，这些末日警告显得遥远且带有鲜明的西方色彩。在他们的认知中，执政党对某项技术失去控制的想法几乎不可思议。此前，官方已成功监管过其他可能引发动荡的技术，其中最典型的当属互联网。在疫情期间，政府通过封锁整个城市并追踪数以亿计的居民展现了其遏制重大危机的强大能力。 “They can immediately cut off the grid of the entire city. They can go to different people to take away their phones. They have an intense amount of power in the physical world,” said Afra Wang, a Silicon Valley-based tech writer focusing on A.I. and technology in China. 专注于中国人工智能与技术领域的硅谷科技作家阿芙拉·王（音）表示：“他们可以立即切断整个城市的电网，可以随时查没个人的手机。他们在物理世界中拥有巨大的掌控力。” “Given this amount of control over its people,” she said, how does one convince the party “that something like A.I. that lives on a computer is scary?” “鉴于党对社会拥有如此强效的控制，”她说，要如何让党相信“运行在电脑里的AI令人恐惧？” 2022年在北京，关停店铺周围设立的金属隔离栏。新冠疫情展现出，官方能够多迅速地封锁整座城市并利用大规模数字监控追踪数以亿计的居民。 In more cynical readings, the apocalyptic warnings sound like a ploy to stop Chinese A.I. companies from overtaking their U.S. rivals, with Chinese media reports suggesting that American A.I. companies are using “fear marketing” to maintain their market lead. 一种更为审慎的解读认为，此类末日警告听起来像是阻止中国人工智能企业超越美国对手的策略。中国媒体就有报道指出，美国人工智能企业正通过“恐惧营销”来维持其市场领先地位。 “In domestic industry circles, or among the people around me, most simply tune out,” said Jie Cai, who until recently was researching human-computer interaction technology and A.I. safety at Tsinghua University. To many in the industry, existential risk seems like a distant priority, he said. “在国内行业圈或我身边的同行中，大多数人对此根本不予理会，”蔡杰说，他此前一直在清华大学从事人机交互技术和人工智能安全方面的研究。在他看来，对行业内许多人而言，关乎存亡的风险是一个极其遥远的议题。 “We still view A.I. as being in a very early stage,” he said. “The focus remains squarely on opportunity and innovation.” “我们依然认为AI处于非常早期的阶段，”他指出。“大家的焦点依然完全集中在机遇与创新上。” For some, A.I. doomerism, with its idea of a looming apocalypse and reckoning for man, seems overtly Christian and especially foreign. One blogger compared Western A.I. fears to novels like Mary Shelley’s “Frankenstein” and the motif that man is punished for trying to create life, the exclusive domain of God. 对部分人而言，人工智能末日论及其蕴含的末日降临与人类审判等观念带有鲜明的基督教色彩，显得极其陌生。一位博主将西方对人工智能的恐惧与玛丽·雪莱的小说《弗兰肯斯坦》中人类因试图挑战神明独有的造物权受惩罚的主题相提并论。 “This narrative tradition does not exist in Chinese culture,” the blogger concluded. 这名博主总结道：“这种叙事传统在中国文化中并不存在。” Liang Fang, head of A.I. safety and governance at Concordia, an A.I. safety consultancy based in Beijing, said that Chinese concepts of heaven or God could also account for how differently the technology was viewed. 总部位于北京的人工智能安全咨询机构安远AI(Concordia)的AI安全与治理主管方亮指出，中国传统的“天”或神的观念也能解释双方在对待该技术时的巨大差异。 He said that Chinese culture emphasized the “oneness of heaven and humanity” and the idea that man was an integral part of nature. “All things, including A.I., come from nature,” he said. “So technology is seen more as a companion in coexistence than an outside force destined to bring destruction.” 他表示，中国文化强调“天人合一”，主张人是自然不可分割的一部分。“万物（包括AI）均来自自然，”他说，“因此，技术更多被视为共存的伙伴，而非注定带来毁灭的外来力量。” 上周四，特朗普总统与中国最高领导人习近平在白宫。部分科技高管与官员警告称，人工智能对人类构成生存威胁，并呼吁北京与华盛顿开展合作。 Even so, the release of Mythos, a powerful Anthropic frontier A.I. model, and others like it has been met in China with concern. Officials have issued new guidelines and warnings about A.I. agents going rogue, being exploited by hackers or used to make biological weapons. 尽管如此，Mythos以及其他类似模型的发布在中国仍引发了担忧，Mythos是来自Anthropic的一款强大的前沿人工智能模型。官方已出台新指南并发出警告，防范人工智能体失控、被黑客利用或被用于制造生物武器。 Officials have drafted a cybercrime law that would require A.I. companies to monitor and stop their models from being used to create malicious code that could be used for cyberattacks. 监管部门已草拟一项网络犯罪法，要求人工智能公司建立监控机制，防止其模型被用于生成攻击性的恶意代码。 The authorities also released an update this month of China’s “A.I. Safety Governance Framework,” a document that is a reliable indicator of future regulation. It echoed some of Silicon Valley’s fears about “recursive self-improvement,” or R.S.I., when A.I. systems are powerful enough to improve themselves with little or no help from human developers and could spin out of control. 官方本月还更新发布了中国《人工智能安全治理框架》，是未来监管走向的重要风向标。该框架回应了硅谷关于“递归自我改进”(RSI)的担忧——即当人工智能系统足够强大，能够在极少或无需人类开发者干预的情况下实现自我迭代时，可能导致系统彻底脱控。 Earlier this month, Wang Lihong, a senior official at the Cyberspace Administration of China, the internet regulator, said that A.I. powered cyberattacks had rendered traditional defense systems obsolete. “High vigilance is urgently needed regarding the risks of extreme A.I. loss of control,” she said. 本月早些时候，国家互联网信息办公室高级官员王丽宏指出，由人工智能驱动的网络攻击已使传统防御体系形同虚设。她强调：“对极端的AI失控风险迫切需要保持高度警惕。” Some Chinese researchers have for years been warning about the risks of A.I. advancing too quickly. In 2024, Pan Xudong and other researchers from Fudan University in Shanghai found that two popular large language models by Meta and Alibaba had shown the ability to replicate themselves, which is seen as a step toward A.I. being able to outsmart human beings.. 一些中国研究人员多年来一直在预警人工智能发展过快的风险。2024年，复旦大学潘旭东团队研究发现，Meta与阿里巴巴的两款主流大语言模型已展现出自我复制的能力，这被视为人工智能超越人类的重要一步。 今年7月在上海举行的世界人工智能大会。 Speaking about the paper at a conference on A.I. safety last year, Mr. Pan said he and his co-authors “wanted to convey that such an extreme A.I. risk is no longer confined to the realm of science fiction but is a real issue demanding discussion and scrutiny.” 去年在一次人工智能安全学术会议上介绍该研究时，潘旭东表示，他和他的论文合著者“希望让大家真正地关注到这个风险，就是说，这样一个极端的人工智能不再是存在于科幻里，它是真正需要大家不断去讨论和关注的”。 But ultimately, in Beijing’s eyes, A.I. is like any other technology that with careful planning can be a powerful force harnessed for the good of the country. China already has some of the world’s strictest regulations on the industry. A.I. produced content must be labeled. A.I. models must be registered and approved by the authorities before being released. 但归根结底，在北京看来，人工智能与任何其他技术无异，只要经过周密规划，就能转化为服务于国家发展的强大力量。中国已出台了全球最严格的行业监管规定，明确要求人工智能生成内容必须进行标识，且人工智能模型在公开发布前必须通过官方备案与审批。 While China has extensive regulation and testing requirements, there is no legal requirement to test for catastrophic risks like an A.I. system being used to make chemical or biological weapons. 尽管中国建立了广泛的监管与测试体系，但在法律层面，尚未对人工智能系统被用于制造化学或生物武器等灾难性风险设定强制测试要求。 Chinese A.I. companies are not as transparent as U.S. firms about their safety measures. Not all of them publish the results of safety evaluations before models are released. Those that do provide less detail and report less frequently than their U.S. peers, according to Concordia, which found that only five of China’s 10 leading A.I. companies reported the results of such evaluations between June 2025 and May 2026. 中国人工智能企业在安全举措的透明度上尚不及美国同行，并非所有企业都会在模型发布前公布安全评估结果。据安远AI统计，公布评估结果的企业在信息详尽度与报告频率上均存在差距；在2025年6月至2026年5月期间，中国前十大人工智能企业中仅有五家公开了相关评估结果。 Sarah Sun, a Shanghai-based founder of the Open Community for AI Safety China, said the U.S. debate about A.I’s threats had helped inspire discussion in China. 总部位于上海的“中国AI安全开放社区”创始人莎拉·孙（音）认为，美国关于AI威胁的讨论客观上推动了中国本土的相关探讨。 But she noted that the Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei’s criticism of China had set off a backlash. In an open letter about the dangers of A.I., Mr. Amodei said that democracies needed to maintain their lead in the technology over authoritarian countries like China. He called for further restricting China’s access to advanced chips and other equipment needed to develop A.I. 但她同时指出，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪对中国的强硬言论引发了反弹。阿莫迪在一封关于人工智能危险性的公开信中宣称，民主国家必须在人工智能技术上保持对中国等威权国家的领先，并呼吁进一步限制中国获取开发人工智能所需的先进芯片及关键设备。 “The fact that Dario has been so hawkish was really, really unhelpful in this scenario,” Ms. Sun said. 莎拉·孙表示：“达里奥如此鹰派的姿态在此情境下适得其反。” This kind of messaging, she said, makes the recent warnings about A.I. seem more like justification for holding China back than genuine concern about catastrophic risk. And that makes it harder for people like her to raise awareness about A.I. safety in China. 她指出，此类言论让近期关于人工智能的警告看起来更像是遏制中国发展的借口，而非对灾难性风险的真诚关切，这直接增加了他们在中国推广人工智能安全意识的难度。 “There are people in China who are genuinely concerned about frontier A.I. risks,” she said, “and are interested in safety” and coordinating international responses. 她还说，“中国确实有一批人深切关注前沿人工智能风险，并致力于推动安全研究及国际协同。” 上周三，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪在联合国大会发表讲话。 Indeed, online commentators in China have referred to Anthropic as “A-chu,” a derogatory term that likens the A.I. giant to a beast. Yuyuan Tantian, a blog linked to China’s state broadcaster, said of American tech leaders like Mr. Amodei that “the only thing they want to slow is the pace at which others catch up.” 事实上，中国网络评论已将Anthropic贬称为“A畜”。官方背景的博客“玉渊潭天”针对阿莫迪等美国科技领袖直言：“他们唯一想放慢的是别人赶超的脚步。” Zhou Hongyi, an influential Chinese cybersecurity executive, has said the solution is not to slow down but to accelerate one’s defensive capabilities with A.I. “Use A.I. to defeat A.I.,” he said in a video posted online last week. “If you use A.I. to attack, I will use A.I. to defend. If you deploy swarms of intelligent agents, I will counter with security agents.” 中国知名网络安全高管周鸿祎表示，应对之道绝非放慢脚步，而是借力人工智能提升防御能力。他在上周发布于网络的一段视频中指出：“用AI打败AI。你用AI攻击，我就用AI防守；你用智能体蜂群，我就用安全智能体跟你对抗。” In an online post earlier this month, an engineer for the Chinese A.I. start-up DeepSeek said that allowing Anthropic to monopolize the world’s most advanced A.I. tools would be “no less serious” than Hitler having acquired the technology for the atomic bomb first in World War II. 本月早些时候，中国人工智能初创企业DeepSeek的一名工程师在一篇网文中写道，允许Anthropic垄断全球最先进的人工智能工具，其严重程度“不亚于”二战时期希特勒率先掌握原子弹技术。 Against this backdrop, it seemed even more unlikely that any agreement between the United States and China to discuss A.I. safety would lead to concrete changes, even if China’s leader, Xi Jinping, told President Trump in Washington that they should “manage A.I. for good.” 在此背景下，即使中国领导人习近平在华盛顿曾向特朗普总统提出两国应“善用人工智能”，中美之间就人工智能安全达成任何协议并推动实质变革的前景依然渺茫。 “If the U.S. says it’s slowing down, China won’t trust that,” said Zhao Minghao, deputy director of the Center for American Studies at Fudan University. “If China says it’s slowing down, the U.S. won’t trust that either.” 复旦大学美国研究中心副主任赵明昊总结道：“如果美国声称要放慢脚步，中国不会相信；如果中国声称要放慢脚步，美国也同样不会相信。” Pei-Lin Wu对本文有报道贡献。 郭莉莉(Lily Kuo)是《纽约时报》报道中国记者，常驻台北。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

During the pandemic, the government showed its ability to contain major crises by locking down entire cities and tracking hundreds of millions of residents. 然而对许多中国民众而言，这些末日警告显得遥远且带有鲜明的西方色彩。在他们的认知中，执政党对某项技术失去控制的想法几乎不可思议。此前，官方已成功监管过其他可能引发动荡的技术，其中最典型的当属互联网。在疫情期间，政府通过封锁整个城市并追踪数以亿计的居民展现了其遏制重大危机的强大能力。 “They can immediately cut off the grid of the entire city. They can go to different people to take away their phones. They have an intense amount of power in the physical world,” said Afra Wang, a Silicon Valley-based tech writer focusing on A.I. and technology in China. 专注于中国人工智能与技术领域的硅谷科技作家阿芙拉·王（音）表示：“他们可以立即切断整个城市的电网，可以随时查没个人的手机。他们在物理世界中拥有巨大的掌控力。” “Given this amount of control over its people,” she said, how does one convince the party “that something like A.I. that lives on a computer is scary?” “鉴于党对社会拥有如此强效的控制，”她说，要如何让党相信“运行在电脑里的AI令人恐惧？” 2022年在北京，关停店铺周围设立的金属隔离栏。新冠疫情展现出，官方能够多迅速地封锁整座城市并利用大规模数字监控追踪数以亿计的居民。 In more cynical readings, the apocalyptic warnings sound like a ploy to stop Chinese A.I. companies from overtaking their U.S. rivals, with Chinese media reports suggesting that American A.I. companies are using “fear marketing” to maintain their market lead. 一种更为审慎的解读认为，此类末日警告听起来像是阻止中国人工智能企业超越美国对手的策略。中国媒体就有报道指出，美国人工智能企业正通过“恐惧营销”来维持其市场领先地位。 “In domestic industry circles, or among the people around me, most simply tune out,” said Jie Cai, who until recently was researching human-computer interaction technology and A.I. safety at Tsinghua University. To many in the industry, existential risk seems like a distant priority, he said. “在国内行业圈或我身边的同行中，大多数人对此根本不予理会，”蔡杰说，他此前一直在清华大学从事人机交互技术和人工智能安全方面的研究。在他看来，对行业内许多人而言，关乎存亡的风险是一个极其遥远的议题。 “We still view A.I. as being in a very early stage,” he said. “The focus remains squarely on opportunity and innovation.” “我们依然认为AI处于非常早期的阶段，”他指出。“大家的焦点依然完全集中在机遇与创新上。” For some, A.I. doomerism, with its idea of a looming apocalypse and reckoning for man, seems overtly Christian and especially foreign. One blogger compared Western A.I. fears to novels like Mary Shelley’s “Frankenstein” and the motif that man is punished for trying to create life, the exclusive domain of God. 对部分人而言，人工智能末日论及其蕴含的末日降临与人类审判等观念带有鲜明的基督教色彩，显得极其陌生。一位博主将西方对人工智能的恐惧与玛丽·雪莱的小说《弗兰肯斯坦》中人类因试图挑战神明独有的造物权受惩罚的主题相提并论。 “This narrative tradition does not exist in Chinese culture,” the blogger concluded. 这名博主总结道：“这种叙事传统在中国文化中并不存在。” Liang Fang, head of A.I. safety and governance at Concordia, an A.I. safety consultancy based in Beijing, said that Chinese concepts of heaven or God could also account for how differently the technology was viewed. 总部位于北京的人工智能安全咨询机构安远AI(Concordia)的AI安全与治理主管方亮指出，中国传统的“天”或神的观念也能解释双方在对待该技术时的巨大差异。 He said that Chinese culture emphasized the “oneness of heaven and humanity” and the idea that man was an integral part of nature. “All things, including A.I., come from nature,” he said. “So technology is seen more as a companion in coexistence than an outside force destined to bring destruction.” 他表示，中国文化强调“天人合一”，主张人是自然不可分割的一部分。“万物（包括AI）均来自自然，”他说，“因此，技术更多被视为共存的伙伴，而非注定带来毁灭的外来力量。” 上周四，特朗普总统与中国最高领导人习近平在白宫。部分科技高管与官员警告称，人工智能对人类构成生存威胁，并呼吁北京与华盛顿开展合作。 Even so, the release of Mythos, a powerful Anthropic frontier A.I. model, and others like it has been met in China with concern. Officials have issued new guidelines and warnings about A.I. agents going rogue, being exploited by hackers or used to make biological weapons . 尽管如此，Mythos以及其他类似模型的发布在中国仍引发了担忧，Mythos是来自Anthropic的一款强大的前沿人工智能模型。官方已出台新指南并发出警告，防范人工智能体失控、被黑客利用或被用于 制造生物武器 。 Officials have drafted a cybercrime law that would require A.I. companies to monitor and stop their models from being used to create malicious code that could be used for cyberattacks. 监管部门已草拟一项网络犯罪法，要求人工智能公司建立监控机制，防止其模型被用于生成攻击性的恶意代码。 The authorities also released an update this month of China’s “A.I. Safety Governance Framework,” a document that is a reliable indicator of future regulation. It echoed some of Silicon Valley’s fears about “recursive self-improvement,” or R.S.I., when A.I. systems are powerful enough to improve themselves with little or no help from human developers and could spin out of control. 官方本月还更新发布了中国《人工智能安全治理框架》，是未来监管走向的重要风向标。该框架回应了硅谷关于“递归自我改进”(RSI)的担忧——即当人工智能系统足够强大，能够在极少或无需人类开发者干预的情况下实现自我迭代时，可能导致系统彻底脱控。 Earlier this month, Wang Lihong, a senior official at the Cyberspace Administration of China, the internet regulator, said that A.I. powered cyberattacks had rendered traditional defense systems obsolete. “High vigilance is urgently needed regarding the risks of extreme A.I. loss of control,” she said. 本月早些时候，国家互联网信息办公室高级官员王丽宏指出，由人工智能驱动的网络攻击已使传统防御体系形同虚设。她强调：“对极端的AI失控风险迫切需要保持高度警惕。” Some Chinese researchers have for years been warning about the risks of A.I. advancing too quickly. In 2024, Pan Xudong and other researchers from Fudan University in Shanghai found that two popular large language models by Meta and Alibaba had shown the ability to replicate themselves , which is seen as a step toward A.I. being able to outsmart human beings.. 一些中国研究人员多年来一直在预警人工智能发展过快的风险。2024年，复旦大学潘旭东团队研究发现，Meta与阿里巴巴的两款主流大语言模型已展现出 自我复制的能力 ，这被视为人工智能超越人类的重要一步。 今年7月在上海举行的世界人工智能大会。 Speaking about the paper at a conference on A.I. safety last year, Mr. Pan said he and his co-authors “wanted to convey that such an extreme A.I. risk is no longer confined to the realm of science fiction but is a real issue demanding discussion and scrutiny.” 去年在一次人工智能安全 学术会议上 介绍该研究时，潘旭东表示，他和他的论文合著者“希望让大家真正地关注到这个风险，就是说，这样一个极端的人工智能不再是存在于科幻里，它是真正需要大家不断去讨论和关注的”。 But ultimately, in Beijing’s eyes, A.I. is like any other technology that with careful planning can be a powerful force harnessed for the good of the country. China already has some of the world’s strictest regulations on the industry. A.I. produced content must be labeled. A.I. models must be registered and approved by the authorities before being released. 但归根结底，在北京看来，人工智能与任何其他技术无异，只要经过周密规划，就能转化为服务于国家发展的强大力量。中国已出台了全球最严格的行业监管规定，明确要求人工智能生成内容必须进行标识，且人工智能模型在公开发布前必须通过官方备案与审批。 While China has extensive regulation and testing requirements, there is no legal requirement to test for catastrophic risks like an A.I. system being used to make chemical or biological weapons. 尽管中国建立了广泛的监管与测试体系，但在法律层面，尚未对人工智能系统被用于制造化学或生物武器等灾难性风险设定强制测试要求。 Chinese A.I. companies are not as transparent as U.S. firms about their safety measures. Not all of them publish the results of safety evaluations before models are released. Those that do provide less detail and report less frequently than their U.S. peers, according to Concordia, which found that only five of China’s 10 leading A.I. companies reported the results of such evaluations between June 2025 and May 2026. 中国人工智能企业在安全举措的透明度上尚不及美国同行，并非所有企业都会在模型发布前公布安全评估结果。据安远AI统计，公布评估结果的企业在信息详尽度与报告频率上均存在差距；在2025年6月至2026年5月期间，中国前十大人工智能企业中仅有五家公开了相关评估结果。 Sarah Sun, a Shanghai-based founder of the Open Community for AI Safety China, said the U.S. debate about A.I’s threats had helped inspire discussion in China. 总部位于上海的“中国AI安全开放社区”创始人莎拉·孙（音）认为，美国关于AI威胁的讨论客观上推动了中国本土的相关探讨。 But she noted that the Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei’s criticism of China had set off a backlash. In an open letter about the dangers of A.I. , Mr. Amodei said that democracies needed to maintain their lead in the technology over authoritarian countries like China. He called for further restricting China’s access to advanced chips and other equipment needed to develop A.I. 但她同时指出，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪对中国的强硬言论引发了反弹。阿莫迪在一封关于 人工智能危险性的公开信 中宣称，民主国家必须在人工智能技术上保持对中国等威权国家的领先，并呼吁进一步限制中国获取开发人工智能所需的先进芯片及关键设备。 “The fact that Dario has been so hawkish was really, really unhelpful in this scenario,” Ms. Sun said. 莎拉·孙表示：“达里奥如此鹰派的姿态在此情境下适得其反。” This kind of messaging, she said, makes the recent warnings about A.I. seem more like justification for holding China back than genuine concern about catastrophic risk. And that makes it harder for people like her to raise awareness about A.I. safety in China. 她指出，此类言论让近期关于人工智能的警告看起来更像是遏制中国发展的借口，而非对灾难性风险的真诚关切，这直接增加了他们在中国推广人工智能安全意识的难度。 “There are people in China who are genuinely concerned about frontier A.I. risks,” she said, “and are interested in safety” and coordinating international responses. 她还说，“中国确实有一批人深切关注前沿人工智能风险，并致力于推动安全研究及国际协同。” 上周三，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪在联合国大会发表讲话。 Indeed, online commentators in China have referred to Anthropic as “A-chu,” a derogatory term that likens the A.I. giant to a beast. Yuyuan Tantian, a blog linked to China’s state broadcaster, said of American tech leaders like Mr. Amodei that “the only thing they want to slow is the pace at which others catch up.” 事实上，中国网络评论已将Anthropic贬称为“A畜”。官方背景的博客“玉渊潭天”针对阿莫迪等美国科技领袖直言：“他们唯一想放慢的是别人赶超的脚步。” Zhou Hongyi, an influential Chinese cybersecurity executive, has said the solution is not to slow down but to accelerate one’s defensive capabilities with A.I. “Use A.I. to defeat A.I.,” he said in a video posted online last week. “If you use A.I. to attack, I will use A.I. to defend. If you deploy swarms of intelligent agents, I will counter with security agents.” 中国知名网络安全高管周鸿祎表示，应对之道绝非放慢脚步，而是借力人工智能提升防御能力。他在上周发布于网络的一段 视频 中指出：“用AI打败AI。你用AI攻击，我就用AI防守；你用智能体蜂群，我就用安全智能体跟你对抗。” In an online post earlier this month, an engineer for the Chinese A.I. start-up DeepSeek said that allowing Anthropic to monopolize the world’s most advanced A.I. tools would be “no less serious” than Hitler having acquired the technology for the atomic bomb first in World War II. 本月早些时候，中国人工智能初创企业DeepSeek的一名工程师在一篇 网文中 写道，允许Anthropic垄断全球最先进的人工智能工具，其严重程度“不亚于”二战时期希特勒率先掌握原子弹技术。 Against this backdrop, it seemed even more unlikely that any agreement between the United States and China to discuss A.I. safety would lead to concrete changes, even if China’s leader, Xi Jinping, told President Trump in Washington that they should “manage A.I. for good.” 在此背景下，即使中国领导人习近平在华盛顿曾向特朗普总统提出两国应“善用人工智能”，中美之间就人工智能安全达成任何协议并推动实质变革的前景依然渺茫。 “If the U.S. says it’s slowing down, China won’t trust that,” said Zhao Minghao, deputy director of the Center for American Studies at Fudan University. “If China says it’s slowing down, the U.S. won’t trust that either.” 复旦大学美国研究中心副主任赵明昊总结道：“如果美国声称要放慢脚步，中国不会相信；如果中国声称要放慢脚步，美国也同样不会相信。” Pei-Lin Wu对本文有报道贡献。 郭莉莉( Lily Kuo )是《纽约时报》报道中国记者，常驻台北。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 中国商界领袖缺席白宫国宴，这说明了什么？
items.description: 黄瑞黎2026年9月28日周四，中国领导人习近平携夫人彭丽媛在白宫与特朗普总统和梅拉尼娅·特朗普合影。 Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times When China’s leader, Xi Jinping, traveled to the United States in 2015 for his first state visit, he brought a delegation of Chinese chief executives to meet their American counterparts. 2015年，中国领导人习近平首次对美国进行国事访问时，他随行带了一支由中国企业的负责人组成的代表团，与美国同行会面。 Disputes over human rights, cyberattacks and trade were straining relations. But Washington and Beijing still shared an undeniable common interest: making money in each other’s markets. 当时，人权、网络攻击和贸易争端正在令两国关系日趋紧张。但华盛顿和北京仍有一个不可否认的共同利益：在彼此的市场赚钱。 A decade later, the contrast with this week’s summit between President Trump and Mr. Xi could not be more stark. No prominent Chinese chief executives attended Thursday night’s state dinner at the White House. 十年后，本周特朗普总统与习近平的峰会与之形成了再鲜明不过的对比。周四晚的白宫国宴上，没有一位中国知名企业负责人出席。 “It’s a rather depressing marker of how bad the relationship has gotten,” said Emily Kilcrease, a senior fellow and director at the Center for a New American Security focused on the U.S.-China economic relationship. “这相当令人沮丧地表明两国关系已经恶化到了什么程度，”新美国安全中心高级研究员兼主任、专注于美中经济关系的艾米丽·基尔克里斯说。 “One of the highlights of this summit was supposed to be some level of announcement of commercial deals,” said Ms. Kilcrease, a former deputy assistant U.S. trade representative. “But it seems like we can’t even get to agreement on some of that.” 曾任美国贸易代表副助理的基尔克里斯说：“这次峰会原本的一大看点应该是会在某种程度上宣布一些商业协议。但现在看来，我们甚至连其中一些协议都无法达成一致。” The absence of Chinese business leaders was a small but telling illustration of how thoroughly the economic relationship between the two countries has changed. In 2015, high-profile tech executives were among those traveling with Mr. Xi, including Alibaba’s Jack Ma and Tencent’s Pony Ma. Their companies were expanding rapidly, and both sides saw enormous opportunities in deeper commercial ties. 中国商界领袖的缺席是一个虽小却意味深长的例子，说明两国经济关系已经发生了多么彻底的变化。2015年，随中国领导人出访的人中包括阿里巴巴的马云和腾讯的马化腾等知名科技公司高管。他们的公司当时正在迅速扩张，而中美双方都认为，进一步深化商业联系蕴藏着巨大机遇。 That era is over. 那个时代已经结束。 2015年习近平访美期间，Facebook的马克·扎克伯格等美国企业高管以及马云等中国公司高管为他鼓掌。 Beginning in Mr. Trump’s first term, the two countries have imposed waves of tariffs on each other. Washington restricted access to some of America’s most advanced technology and limited U.S. investments in parts of China’s high-tech sector. The United States slapped 100 percent tariffs and imposed restrictions on internet-connected vehicles from China, making it financially unviable for the country’s electric vehicles to enter the United States. 从特朗普第一任期开始，两国相互加征了一轮又一轮关税。华盛顿限制中国获取美国部分最先进的技术，并限制美国对中国部分高科技行业的投资。美国对来自中国的联网汽车征收100%的关税并实施限制，使中国电动汽车进入美国市场在经济上变得几乎不可能。 Beijing retaliated with its own trade restrictions, including controls on exports of rare-earth metals and rare-earth magnets essential to U.S. manufacturers. 北京则以自己的贸易限制措施予以反击，包括对稀土金属和稀土磁体的出口管制，而这些材料对美国制造商至关重要。 At the same time, Chinese companies have evolved from prospective customers and partners for American businesses into some of their most formidable competitors. 与此同时，中国企业已经从美国企业眼中的潜在客户和合作伙伴变成了它们最难对付的竞争对手之一。 And many of China’s most prominent entrepreneurs now come from industries like artificial intelligence, robotics and electric vehicles — the exact technologies Washington and Beijing are competing most intensely for. 中国许多最杰出的企业家如今来自人工智能、机器人技术和电动汽车等行业，恰恰也是华盛顿和北京竞争最激烈的那些技术领域。 It would be difficult to imagine, for example, seeing the DeepSeek co-founder Liang Wenfeng showcased alongside the OpenAI chief executive, Sam Altman, at a state dinner. 举例来说，难以想像在一场国宴上，DeepSeek联合创始人梁文锋会与OpenAI首席执行官山姆·奥特曼一起亮相。 Yet until days before the summit, Chinese officials expected they might bring a business delegation to Washington, according to two people familiar with the discussions who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to disclose details of the private conversations. 然而，据两名知情人士透露，直到峰会前几天，中国官员仍预计可能会带一支商业代表团前往华盛顿。由于无权披露这些私人谈话的细节，两人要求匿名。 It was unclear which executives were under consideration, although reports had mentioned Wang Chuanfu, founder of the electric carmaker BYD, and Robin Zeng, chief executive of the battery maker CATL. Their presence would have allowed Mr. Xi to highlight China’s dominance in battery technology and renewable energy. 目前尚不清楚哪些高管曾被考虑，但有报道提到电动汽车制造商比亚迪创始人王传福和电池制造商宁德时代首席执行官曾毓群。他们的出席本有助于习近平强调中国在电池技术和可再生能源领域的主导地位。 In the end, none received invitations. 最终，没有人收到邀请。 周四，埃隆·马斯克与特朗普夫人在国宴上。 Several top Chinese executives arrived in Washington shortly before the summit and held meetings outside the official gathering. 多位中国顶级高管在峰会前不久抵达华盛顿，并在官方聚会之外举行了会议。 “There are a number of important Chinese C.E.O.s in Washington, waiting on the sidelines, like: ‘Do I get tapped or not?’” said Jeremy Chan, a senior China analyst at Eurasia Group and a former American diplomat who worked in China. “The whole thing is crazy. It would be comical if it weren’t so tragic.” “华盛顿有多位重要的中国企业首席执行官在场外观望，心里都在想：‘会不会叫到我？’”欧亚集团的中国问题高级分析师、曾在中国工作的前美国外交官杰里米·陈（音）说。“整件事太疯狂了。要不是因为太可悲，这件事甚至显得有点滑稽。” There was another complication: Some prominent Chinese companies face U.S. restrictions, making their appearance at a White House state dinner politically fraught. In June, the U.S. Department of Defense had included Alibaba and BYD in its expanded list of firms it identified as “Chinese military companies.” 还有另一个复杂因素：一些中国知名企业受到美国方面的限制，相关企业的负责人如果出现在白宫国宴上，在政治上会相当棘手。今年6月，美国国防部把阿里巴巴和比亚迪列入了扩大后的所谓“中国军工企业”名单。 “It would actually be seen by some in Washington as provocative to bring these companies along,” said Ilaria Mazzocco, a deputy director at the Center for Strategic and International Studies specializing in Chinese business and economics. 专门研究中国商业和经济问题的战略与国际研究中心副主任伊拉里娅·马佐科说：“让这些公司参与进来实际上会被华盛顿一些人视为挑衅。” The contrast was especially striking compared with the scene when Mr. Trump visited Beijing in May. 与特朗普今年5月访问北京时的场面相比，这种反差尤其鲜明。 Apple’s Tim Cook, Tesla’s Elon Musk and other executives of top American companies stood on the steps of Beijing’s Great Hall of the People just behind senior U.S. officials. Mr. Trump told Mr. Xi that he had brought “the greatest businessmen, the biggest, and I guess the best, in the world.” 苹果的蒂姆·库克、特斯拉的埃隆·马斯克以及其他美国顶尖企业的高管站在北京人民大会堂的台阶上，紧挨在美国高级官员身后。特朗普对中国领导人说，他带来了“世界上最伟大的商人，最了不起的，我想也是最优秀的”。 Mr. Trump added, “I didn’t want the second or the third in the company, I wanted only the top, and they’re here today to pay respects to you and to China.” 特朗普还说：“我不要公司的二三把手，我要第一把手，所以他们都来了，表示出对中国和对您的尊重。” 今年5月特朗普访问北京期间，时任苹果首席执行官的蒂姆·库克出席欢迎仪式。 On Thursday, many of the same executives from U.S. firms were present again. Alongside Mr. Cook and Mr. Musk were Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Amazon’s Jeff Bezos, OpenAI’s Mr. Altman, Microsoft’s Satya Nadella and General Motors’ Mary Barra. 周四，不少来自同一批美国企业的高管再次出席。与库克和马斯克一同在场的还有英伟达的黄仁勋、Meta的马克·扎克伯格、亚马逊的杰夫·贝索斯、OpenAI的奥特曼、微软的萨蒂亚·纳德拉和通用汽车的玛丽·博拉。 Earlier in the day, Mr. Xi said in a speech that China “welcomes American companies wanting to invest and do business there.” Then, in an apparent reference to the U.S. restrictions on Chinese firms operating in America, he added: “We hope Chinese companies are treated fairly here in the United States.” 当天早些时候，习近平在讲话中说，中国“欢迎美国企业来华投资兴业”。随后，他显然是暗指美国对中国企业在美运营的限制，又补充说：“希望美方公平对待中国企业。” While American companies have not given up on China, they are struggling to compete against its companies. Nike is battling increasingly popular Chinese brands. 虽然美国企业并没有放弃中国市场，但它们正越来越难以与中国企业竞争。美国汽车制造商已经在与中国电动汽车制造商的竞争中节节败退。苹果正面临华为的激烈竞争。耐克也在应对越来越受欢迎的中国品牌的挑战。 Yet China remains too large and too deeply embedded in global manufacturing for many American companies to ignore. So why should they waste their time?” 伍德克说：“中国还有谁有兴趣去美国做生意吗？没有，因为不可能。那他们为什么还要浪费时间？” Ana Swanson和Lauren Hirsch对本文有报道贡献。 黄瑞黎(Sui-Lee Wee)是《纽约时报》东南亚分社社长，负责该地区11个国家的报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
